N5:grammar:supp-question-words-basic.notes: 何 (なに/なん) asks what; 誰 (だれ) who; どこ where; いつ when; どう how or what something is like; どうして/なぜ why. Learn readings with constructions: 何ですか uses なん and 何を uses なに. Many number/counter expressions use なん. 何人 is なんにん for how many people but なにじん for nationality, so the following sound alone is not a complete rule. Put the question word in the unknown information position and retain the particle needed for its role, e.g. 誰が来ましたか.
N5:grammar:supp-question-words-basic.review_note: Removed categorical nani/nan sound-only rule; added counter/nationality distinction from ARC Tokyo teacher explanation: https://arc.ac.jp/Tokyo/mimi-bunpou088/ (2025-02-19), checked 2026-10-29. No native-speaker review claimed.

N5:grammar:supp-ikutsu-how-many.notes: いくつ asks how many in general object counting and can also ask age; おいくつですか is polite. It is not restricted to round objects. Category-specific forms include 何本, 何枚 and 何人.
N5:grammar:supp-ikutsu-how-many.review_note: Semantic pass068: avoid unsupported shape/AM-PM restrictions and false phonetic terminology; primary references recorded in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-counter-ji-oclock.notes: 時 (じ) counts clock hours, distinct from 時間 for duration. Important readings: 4時 よじ, 7時 しちじ, 9時 くじ. Add 分 for minutes and に for an action at a time. Do not infer AM or PM from an unqualified hour.
N5:grammar:supp-counter-ji-oclock.review_note: Semantic pass068: avoid unsupported shape/AM-PM restrictions and false phonetic terminology; primary references recorded in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-counter-fun-minute.notes: 分 counts clock minutes and durations. Pronunciation varies between ふん and ぷん with possible changes to the preceding numeral; this is not a voiced/voiceless contrast. Common forms: いっぷん, にふん, さんぷん, よんぷん, ごふん, ろっぷん, ななふん, はっぷん (also はちふん), きゅうふん, じゅっぷん (also じっぷん). 半 means half past the hour in clock expressions.
N5:grammar:supp-counter-fun-minute.review_note: Semantic pass068: avoid unsupported shape/AM-PM restrictions and false phonetic terminology; primary references recorded in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-counter-en-money.formation: Number + 円 (えん). The counter stays en; numeral readings can change, e.g. 3000円 さんぜんえん.
N5:grammar:supp-counter-en-money.notes: 円 counts amounts in Japanese yen. The counter itself remains えん, but numerals retain their own reading changes, e.g. さんびゃく and さんぜん. Ask prices with いくらですか or 何円ですか.
N5:grammar:supp-counter-en-money.review_note: Semantic pass069: correct counter-reading scope, full phonetic forms and adjective past formation; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-counter-hon-long.formation: Number + 本: いっぽん, にほん, さんぼん, よんほん, ごほん, ろっぽん, ななほん, はっぽん, きゅうほん, じゅっぽん/じっぽん. Question: なんぼん.
N5:grammar:supp-counter-hon-long.notes: 本 counts long thin objects such as pencils, bottles, umbrellas, trees, bananas, wire and roads; conventional uses include train services, phone calls and films. The counter alternates ほん/ぼん/ぽん. Some combinations also change the preceding numeral and include small っ; ぽん alone is not a geminate consonant.
N5:grammar:supp-counter-hon-long.review_note: Semantic pass069: correct counter-reading scope, full phonetic forms and adjective past formation; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-jikan-time-duration.formation: Number + 時間 (じかん); 1 いちじかん, 4 よじかん, 7 しちじかん/ななじかん, 9 くじかん; question なんじかん.
N5:grammar:supp-jikan-time-duration.notes: 時間 counts elapsed hours, distinct from 時 for clock time. Use it for durations of study, work, travel and sleep. The suffix remains じかん, but numeral readings include special forms such as よじかん and くじかん.
N5:grammar:supp-jikan-time-duration.review_note: Semantic pass069: correct counter-reading scope, full phonetic forms and adjective past formation; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-i-adj-adverbial-ku.notes: Replace final い with く to modify a verb or predicate: 早い→早く, 大きい→大きく, 高い→高く. いい becomes よく. The negative uses くない (高くない); the past instead replaces final い with かった (高かった), not くかった. よく can mean well, a lot or often depending on context.
N5:grammar:supp-i-adj-adverbial-ku.review_note: Semantic pass069: correct counter-reading scope, full phonetic forms and adjective past formation; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-arimasu-existence-inanim.notes: あります expresses existence of objects, plants, abstract matters and events. For physical location in this pattern use place に and entity が. Living people and animals normally use います. An event venue instead can use place で, e.g. an event is held there; do not generalize existential location に to every event use.
N5:grammar:supp-arimasu-existence-inanim.review_note: Semantic pass070: qualify basic existence/event-venue and desire-person rules; field-level semantic basis retained in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-imasu-existence-animate.notes: います normally locates living people and animals; あります normally locates objects and plants. In this existential pattern に marks the location and が the entity. This is a grammatical usage distinction, not a biological classification of all living things.
N5:grammar:supp-imasu-existence-animate.review_note: Semantic pass070: qualify basic existence/event-venue and desire-person rules; field-level semantic basis retained in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-ga-hoshii-wanting-thing.notes: ほしい/欲しい is an i-adjective for wanting things, marked with が; use a verb stem plus たい for wanting to do an action. In ordinary direct assertions it expresses the speakers own desire, or asks the listener about theirs. Third-person desire is normally expressed with ほしがる/ほしがっています or reported with ほしいと言っています; this is not an absolute ban on hoshii in all third-person contexts.
N5:grammar:supp-ga-hoshii-wanting-thing.review_note: Semantic pass070: qualify basic existence/event-venue and desire-person rules; field-level semantic basis retained in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-mou-ta-already.notes: With a completed past-tense action, もう means already: completion before a reference time. For not yet completed, まだ commonly combines with Vていない/ていません, a negative te-iru form, not necessarily a progressive action. This differs from merely denying a past event. Other uses of もう have other meanings.
N5:grammar:supp-mou-ta-already.review_note: Semantic pass071: clarify relative completion, te-iru non-completion and superlative predicate scope; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-mada-not-yet.notes: まだ can mean not yet with Vていない/ていません, or still with an ongoing action/state such as Vている/ています. The negative te-iru form here expresses non-completion, not necessarily an ongoing progressive. まだ also combines with other predicates, e.g. まだあります (still exists). A simple past negative is not interchangeable with the standard not-yet-completed expression.
N5:grammar:supp-mada-not-yet.review_note: Semantic pass071: clarify relative completion, te-iru non-completion and superlative predicate scope; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:supp-toki-ni-when-basic.notes: とき locates the main-clause event in time; に is optional. Verb forms may express relative completion: V nonpast とき before completion/when about to do it, V past とき after completion/when it has happened, depending on verb and context. Ongoing action uses Vているとき. Main-clause tense sets overall time; do not equate a nonpast toki clause with present time or a bare past form with was doing. Noun の and na-adjective な precede とき.
N5:grammar:supp-toki-ni-when-basic.review_note: Semantic pass071: clarify relative completion, te-iru non-completion and superlative predicate scope; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:hana-54f5e5c93415.meaning: Express the highest degree of the following quality or action: the most / the best; the least only with a low-quantity quality such as 少ない.
N5:grammar:hana-54f5e5c93415.formation: Noun + が + 一番 + adjective predicate; a topic may use は. Before a verb use the appropriate adverbial expression, e.g. 一番速く泳げます.
N5:grammar:hana-54f5e5c93415.notes: 一番 marks the highest degree within the comparison group; the following predicate determines the quality. 一番少ない is least because 少ない means few/little; 一番 alone does not mean least. で/の中で specifies scope. With verbs an adverb may specify the comparison, and potential 泳げます retains can swim.
N5:grammar:hana-54f5e5c93415.review_note: Semantic pass071: clarify relative completion, te-iru non-completion and superlative predicate scope; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:hana-703908db5d04.formation: A と B と どっち + suitable particle が/を etc. + predicate. A か B か、どっち... is another alternative-question construction.
N5:grammar:hana-703908db5d04.notes: どっち is the casual counterpart of どちら, asking which of two options. It combines with the particle required by the predicate, e.g. が好き, を買う. AかBか is an alternative question structure, not merely a shortened spelling of AとBと.

N5:grammar:hana-94ba4c85b4cc.meaning: Deliberately make something have the quality of an i-adjective.
N5:grammar:hana-94ba4c85b4cc.formation: (Object を +) i-adjective with final い replaced by く + します; いい→よくします.
N5:grammar:hana-94ba4c85b4cc.notes: くします expresses an agent making a quality or state change, unlike くなります for becoming/changing state. Do not translate shimasu as uncaused become or as can. Depending on context it can describe a present action or future intention.
N5:grammar:hana-94ba4c85b4cc.review_note: Semantic pass073: distinguish caused results and noun choice; allow mixed adjective classes in joining; field evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:hana-c5f2f70d3077.meaning: Join descriptions using the くて form of an i-adjective.
N5:grammar:hana-c5f2f70d3077.formation: Replace final い with くて + following description/predicate; いい→よくて.
N5:grammar:hana-c5f2f70d3077.notes: The first i-adjective uses くて to link descriptions. The following predicate need not be an i-adjective: 感動的 in the movie example is a na-adjective. The final predicate carries overall tense and politeness.
N5:grammar:hana-c5f2f70d3077.review_note: Semantic pass073: distinguish caused results and noun choice; allow mixed adjective classes in joining; field evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:hana-506ae7093495.meaning: Make or set a state with a na-adjective; distinguish noun にします for choosing.
N5:grammar:hana-506ae7093495.formation: (Object を +) na-adjective stem + にします. Choice: noun phrase + にします.
N5:grammar:hana-506ae7093495.notes: Na-adjective stem にします expresses making/setting a state, e.g. quiet or clean, distinct from になります for becoming. The final example 健康的な食事にします has the noun phrase 健康的な食事 before にします and means choose a healthy meal; it is not a direct na-adjective-to-adverb transformation.
N5:grammar:hana-506ae7093495.review_note: Semantic pass073: distinguish caused results and noun choice; allow mixed adjective classes in joining; field evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:hana-ca9785f3638f.pattern: Noun/Clause A か Noun/Clause B (か)
N5:grammar:hana-ca9785f3638f.formation: Noun A か noun B (final か may occur); plain-form clause A か plain-form clause B か for alternative actions.
N5:grammar:hana-ca9785f3638f.notes: か links alternatives, including noun phrases and verbal clauses. The final か is not mandatory in every noun-list context, as 電車かバスを uses one linker. One-only selection and a not-yet decision are supplied by the rest of the sentence, not by か itself.
N5:grammar:hana-ca9785f3638f.review_note: Semantic pass074: align range, approximation, alternatives and decision details to Japanese; evidence in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:hana-53b90e0dcd0a.formation: ます-stem + たいです: 食べます→食べたいです, 行きます→行きたいです, します→したいです, 来ます→来たいです (きたいです). Not every verb ending in る is ichidan: 帰る→帰りたいです.
N5:grammar:hana-53b90e0dcd0a.notes: たい expresses wanting to do an action and inflects like an i-adjective. It normally expresses the speakers own desire directly; third-person statements require suitable context/evidence and often use reported たいと言っています or observable たがっています. Do not form every る-ending verb by removing る; use the masu-stem rule, including kuru→kitai.

N5:grammar:hana-b4874f4038ce.notes: Dictionary-form verb + こと nominalizes the action as a concept. Dictionary form is not restricted to verbs ending in る: 泳ぐ, 話す and 歌う also occur. Particles such as は or が then place the nominalized action in the sentence.

N5:grammar:hana-4fc32fcc0ba6.notes: Dictionary-form verb + ことができます expresses ability or possibility through nominalization with こと. It is not the verb-inflection potential form itself. The negative is ことができません; all dictionary-form verbs can be used, not only る-ending verbs.

N5:grammar:hana-ed3d21dedf4e.notes: Dictionary-form verb + ことができる expresses ability/possibility, with polite できます and connective できて. This is a construction, not a verb-inflection potential form. Dictionary forms need not end in る, e.g. 解く, 泳ぐ, 行く, 弾く.

N5:grammar:hana-c17bdfc1324c.meaning: A conversational sentence-final explanatory の; distinguish nominalizing の and explicit purpose/reason clauses.
N5:grammar:hana-c17bdfc1324c.formation: Plain-form verb + sentence-final の; polite explanatory のです/んです.
N5:grammar:hana-c17bdfc1324c.notes: All examples here have explanatory sentence-final の. The purpose in example1 is marked by ために, and reasons in the other examples by ので. Sentence-final の is not itself a purpose/reason conjunction. Nominalizing の as in のが好き is a separate syntactic use.
N5:grammar:hana-c17bdfc1324c.review_note: Semantic pass076: align constructions and predicate polarity; ambiguity retained explicitly in review-ledger.jsonl and unresolved-example-senses.json.

N5:grammar:hana-134874b5f296.meaning: Before doing an action or before an event.
N5:grammar:hana-134874b5f296.notes: Dictionary-form verb + 前に indicates that the main-clause action precedes that verb event. It does not itself impose obligation; requests, instructions and suggestions come from the main predicate.
N5:grammar:hana-134874b5f296.review_note: Semantic pass076: align constructions and predicate polarity; ambiguity retained explicitly in review-ledger.jsonl and unresolved-example-senses.json.

N5:grammar:hana-e76c3790e5cc.formation: あまり + negative verb (ません / ないです); i-adjective くありません / くないです; na-adjective ではありません / じゃないです; existence がありません.
N5:grammar:hana-e76c3790e5cc.notes: With a negative predicate, あまり indicates low degree, frequency or amount, not necessarily zero. Do not append ありません to a complete verb ない form. Example2 is now an explicitly authored morning-waking context: early, not speed. The underspecified original is archived.

N5:grammar:hana-483e8ddc49d4.formation: Giver から/に + thing を + もらいます; action benefit: actor に + Vて + もらいます.
N5:grammar:hana-483e8ddc49d4.notes: もらいます describes receiving from the receiver perspective. Vてもらいます describes receiving a benefit from an action done by another person. Actor に is the basic form for action benefits; から cannot simply replace に for every verb. This is not merely allowing someone to act or necessarily forcing them.
N5:grammar:hana-483e8ddc49d4.review_note: Semantic pass077: align source roles, auxiliary connection and copula; original error and correction recorded in review-ledger.jsonl.

N5:grammar:hana-1739f404f703.formation: Giver が + 私に + thing を + くれます; action benefit: giver が + Vて + くれます (beneficiary follows the verbs argument structure).
N5:grammar:hana-1739f404f703.notes: くれます presents giving toward the speaker or the speakers in-group. For action benefits Vて directly connects to くれます. Do not insert 私に between the te-form and auxiliary; place the beneficiary appropriately in the clause.

N5:grammar:hana-4eda4e08e1c4.formation: どちらが + predicate; どちらを + verb; どちらに + movement/selection verb; どちらの + noun.
N5:grammar:hana-4eda4e08e1c4.notes: In this lesson, ask which of two choices or compare two things. Select particles by syntactic role; do not place を before every adjective or noun predicate. の links どちら to a following noun.
N5:grammar:hana-4eda4e08e1c4.review_note: Semantic pass081: destination negation, hand-fan/ramen senses, polite WHO, two-way choice and which/whichever. Three underspecified examples remain pending in unresolved-example-senses.json; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-664fa7701349.formation: どなたが / どなたですか; どなたか + request; どなたも + predicate.
N5:grammar:hana-664fa7701349.notes: どなた is polite だれ (who), not what or where. どなたか is someone. With affirmative 知っている here, どなたも means everyone; with a negative predicate it means nobody.
N5:grammar:hana-664fa7701349.review_note: Semantic pass081: destination negation, hand-fan/ramen senses, polite WHO, two-way choice and which/whichever. Three underspecified examples remain pending in unresolved-example-senses.json; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-9a18fcd1ce12.formation: どの + noun, followed by a case particle appropriate to its role.
N5:grammar:hana-9a18fcd1ce12.notes: どの is an attributive interrogative modifying the following noun, unlike standalone どれ. Do not teach it as an independently usable question word ど plus an ordinary linking particle の.
N5:grammar:hana-9a18fcd1ce12.review_note: Semantic pass081: destination negation, hand-fan/ramen senses, polite WHO, two-way choice and which/whichever. Three underspecified examples remain pending in unresolved-example-senses.json; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-c9afa8e84b9c.formation: どれでも + predicate, e.g. いいです / おいしいです / 選んでください.
N5:grammar:hana-c9afa8e84b9c.notes: Any or whichever of the available items. どれでもおいしい means whichever one is chosen is delicious. だれでも, いつでも and どこでも are parallel forms for other referents, not additions attached to どれでも.
N5:grammar:hana-c9afa8e84b9c.review_note: Semantic pass081: destination negation, hand-fan/ramen senses, polite WHO, two-way choice and which/whichever. Three underspecified examples remain pending in unresolved-example-senses.json; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-1e79f33dc4a5.formation: なにか + (appropriate particle) + predicate; optionally specify with a noun or an adjective+noun phrase.
N5:grammar:hana-1e79f33dc4a5.notes: An indefinite thing. It can stand independently (なにかあります) and is not restricted to modifying a following noun. Particles follow wh+か; が/を may be omitted. Preserve conditionals and 遠慮なく (without hesitation).
N5:grammar:hana-1e79f33dc4a5.review_note: Semantic pass082: what-kind, indefinite things, total negation, nan/nande, anything and naming. なんで来ましたか remains provisional; final cafeteria example syntax explicitly repaired with original retained. AI semantic review, no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-99e8c357bf07.formation: なにも + verb masu-stem + ません; past negative ませんでした.
N5:grammar:hana-99e8c357bf07.notes: Remove ます before adding ません. Total object negation does not inherently mean inability: 食べませんでした is did not eat; 見えません describes lack of visibility.
N5:grammar:hana-99e8c357bf07.review_note: Semantic pass082: what-kind, indefinite things, total negation, nan/nande, anything and naming. なんで来ましたか remains provisional; final cafeteria example syntax explicitly repaired with original retained. AI semantic review, no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-fff6cd308373.meaning: What, or how many/how old with an appropriate counter: the なん reading of 何.

N5:grammar:hana-a2850394284d.formation: Giver は/が + receiver に + thing を + あげます.
N5:grammar:hana-a2850394284d.notes: Giving is viewed from the giver; に marks the recipient and を the thing. If the speaker is the recipient, use an appropriate くれます/もらいます construction. あげましょう proposes giving; あげたい expresses desire to give.

N5:grammar:hana-faf9933075ee.notes: Receiver/beneficiary is subject; に marks giver or performer. Vてもらう presents a service as benefiting that subject. The authored maternal-grandmother example explicitly says 母の母; original obaasan ambiguity is archived, not guessed.

N5:grammar:hana-180072f0dc7d.formation: Noun は たいへんです; dictionary-form verb + のはたいへんです.
N5:grammar:hana-180072f0dc7d.notes: Describes difficulty or burden in handling a task/situation. A verb phrase can become the topic through の. In this lesson たいへんです is a predicate, not the separate adverbial very use.

N5:grammar:hana-9852d83fab73.formation: ほとんど + predicate; ほとんどの + noun; ほとんど + negative predicate.
N5:grammar:hana-9852d83fab73.notes: With affirmative predicates, almost complete or almost all. With negative predicates, a very low degree/quantity/frequency, not necessarily total zero. Use の before the noun in ほとんどの人. Preserve the passed-test result in the third example.
N5:grammar:hana-9852d83fab73.review_note: Semantic pass083: giver/receiver roles, task difficulty, nearly all versus hardly, moderate evaluation and still/not yet. Obaasan letter example remains pending contextual/kinship review. No native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-a0e2d18d6f16.formation: まあまあです; まあまあ + adjectival predicate.
N5:grammar:hana-a0e2d18d6f16.notes: In these examples, moderately good, so-so or satisfactory rather than outstanding. Not bad is not the same as bad. Preserve the past movie judgment and the subjective I think about her singing skill.
N5:grammar:hana-a0e2d18d6f16.review_note: Semantic pass083: giver/receiver roles, task difficulty, nearly all versus hardly, moderate evaluation and still/not yet. Obaasan letter example remains pending contextual/kinship review. No native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-04d63f7fa707.formation: まだ + appropriately formed predicate, e.g. 食べていません / 暑いです / 学生です / 学生じゃないです.
N5:grammar:hana-04d63f7fa707.notes: Continuation means still; a not-yet-realized event with negative predicate means not yet. Nouns and na-adjectives may also take affirmative predicates; do not restrict them to negatives. Bare verb te-form is not a complete finite predicate.
N5:grammar:hana-04d63f7fa707.review_note: Semantic pass083: giver/receiver roles, task difficulty, nearly all versus hardly, moderate evaluation and still/not yet. Obaasan letter example remains pending contextual/kinship review. No native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-f5c3d9b4a1f5.formation: まだ + verb negative form + です; also ていないです for a not-yet-realized event/result.
N5:grammar:hana-f5c3d9b4a1f5.notes: The specified event has not yet occurred/completed. It does not imply that nothing at all has occurred or that the action is impossible or will never occur. Preserve homework, coming, film starting and our dinner negatives.
N5:grammar:hana-f5c3d9b4a1f5.review_note: Semantic pass083: giver/receiver roles, task difficulty, nearly all versus hardly, moderate evaluation and still/not yet. Obaasan letter example remains pending contextual/kinship review. No native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-0635ce119adf.formation: まだ + polite negative predicate, e.g. 食べていません / 終わっていません / 行ったことがありません.
N5:grammar:hana-0635ce119adf.notes: Polite register, not political. 終わっていません describes unfinished state, not inability to finish. 行ったことがありません describes lack of experience up to now, not a claim about never going in the future.
N5:grammar:hana-0635ce119adf.review_note: Semantic pass083: giver/receiver roles, task difficulty, nearly all versus hardly, moderate evaluation and still/not yet. Obaasan letter example remains pending contextual/kinship review. No native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-796334edfc7e.formation: もう + appropriately formed predicate, e.g. 食べました / 働かない / 十分です; もうすぐ + upcoming event.
N5:grammar:hana-796334edfc7e.notes: Already for a completed action/changed state; no longer with a negative predicate. In the supplied summer-vacation example, soon comes from もうすぐ. Preserve summer, lunch and negative future work.
N5:grammar:hana-796334edfc7e.review_note: Semantic pass084: already/no longer/soon, comparative more, often versus well, and locative existence. Character gloss review follows N5 grammar. AI semantic review; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-8d3cb3b926c3.formation: もうすぐ + event clause; also event noun + です, e.g. 誕生日です.
N5:grammar:hana-8d3cb3b926c3.notes: The time of an event is approaching, not an event already completed. Not restricted to verb predicates. でしょう in the rain example keeps a likely prediction rather than certainty.
N5:grammar:hana-8d3cb3b926c3.review_note: Semantic pass084: already/no longer/soon, comparative more, often versus well, and locative existence. Character gloss review follows N5 grammar. AI semantic review; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-bb656f5c7c4d.notes: More or further in quantity/degree relative to a comparison. Desire and obligation come from the predicate (たい / なければなりません), not from もっと itself. Preserve larger, quieter and greater skill comparisons.
N5:grammar:hana-bb656f5c7c4d.review_note: Semantic pass084: already/no longer/soon, comparative more, often versus well, and locative existence. Character gloss review follows N5 grammar. AI semantic review; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-ea975c748f51.formation: よく + verb in plain or polite form.
N5:grammar:hana-ea975c748f51.notes: Frequency (often) or manner/evaluation (well), depending on context. The first three examples show frequent actions and a past habit; よくできました praises successful performance. Polite forms are allowed, not only casual verbs.
N5:grammar:hana-ea975c748f51.review_note: Semantic pass084: already/no longer/soon, comparative more, often versus well, and locative existence. Character gloss review follows N5 grammar. AI semantic review; no native-speaker certification.

N5:grammar:hana-3a62299f1319.formation: Place に + existent thing が + あります.
N5:grammar:hana-3a62299f1319.notes: に marks location, が the existent subject, not a direct object. Generally use あります for things/plants and います for people/animals. 池 is a pond, コンビニ a convenience store and 神社 a Shinto shrine.
N5:grammar:hana-3a62299f1319.review_note: Semantic pass084: already/no longer/soon, comparative more, often versus well, and locative existence. Character gloss review follows N5 grammar. AI semantic review; no native-speaker certification.

N4:grammar:ba.formation: All verb groups: final u-row kana to e-row kana + ば (書けば, 食べれば, すれば, 来れば [くれば]); i-adjective: drop い + ければ (いい→よければ); negative ない→なければ; na-adjective/noun + なら(ば) or であれば
N4:grammar:ba.notes: Highlights the condition for a result. Requests or invitations after a volitional action with the same subject are restricted; state predicates or different subjects can permit them. This is not an absolute ban on requests after ば.

corrections.original: Verb-ba / i-Adj stem + ければ / na-Adj + なら / Noun + なら
corrections.replacement: All verb groups: final u-row kana to e-row kana + ば (書けば, 食べれば, すれば, 来れば [くれば]); i-adjective: drop い + ければ (いい→よければ); negative ない→なければ; na-adjective/noun + なら(ば) or であれば

corrections.original: Focuses on the condition needed for a result. When the main clause is a request or invitation, たら is usually more natural unless the ば-clause is a state (ある, いる, adjectives).
corrections.replacement: Highlights the condition for a result. Requests or invitations after a volitional action with the same subject are restricted; state predicates or different subjects can permit them. This is not an absolute ban on requests after ば.

source_corrections.basis: Ba exact conjugation includes ichidan/irregulars, yokereba, negative nakereba and nominal deareba. Preserve condition not garbled negative obligation, cheap not easy, ask not think. Request restrictions depend on state and subjects, not absolute ban.

corrections.original: In Japanese, a full clause can modify a noun by being placed before it in plain form — there is no relative pronoun like 'which' or 'that'. N4:grammar:supp-jidoushi-tadoushi.formation: Transitive object pattern: agent が/は + object を + verb. Intransitive event pattern: event subject が/は + verb. Transitive/intransitive pairs: 開ける/開く, 閉める/閉まる, 始める/始まる, 出す/出る, 入れる/入る, 上げる/上がる, 下げる/下がる, 消す/消える, 付ける/付く, 落とす/落ちる, 止める/止まる, 集める/集まる. Perception contrasts: 見る/見える and 聞く/聞こえる distinguish attending/perceiving from being visible/audible.
N4:grammar:supp-jidoushi-tadoushi.notes: Transitivity is structural: a transitive verb has an object; an intransitive event foregrounds its subject without specifying an external agent. Intransitive does not guarantee spontaneous occurrence and is not passive voice. Subject can be topicalized with は. Not every を marks an object: path or departure を can accompany intransitive motion verbs. 見える/聞こえる are separate perception verbs, not merely the potential inflections of 見る/聞く.

corrections.original: Common pairs (transitive / intransitive): 開ける/開く, 閉める/閉まる, 始める/始まる, 出す/出る, 入れる/入る, 上げる/上がる, 下げる/下がる, 見る/見える, 聞く/聞こえる, 消す/消える, 付ける/付く, 落とす/落ちる, 止める/止まる, 集める/集まる.
corrections.replacement: Transitive object pattern: agent が/は + object を + verb. Intransitive event pattern: event subject が/は + verb. Transitive/intransitive pairs: 開ける/開く, 閉める/閉まる, 始める/始まる, 出す/出る, 入れる/入る, 上げる/上がる, 下げる/下がる, 消す/消える, 付ける/付く, 落とす/落ちる, 止める/止まる, 集める/集まる. Perception contrasts: 見る/見える and 聞く/聞こえる distinguish attending/perceiving from being visible/audible.

The distinction is structural: transitive verbs take を for their object; intransitive verbs take が for the thing undergoing the action. Learning the pair patterns is essential to reading comprehension and to using the 〜ている / 〜てある state-of-affairs distinction correctly.
corrections.replacement: Transitivity is structural: a transitive verb has an object; an intransitive event foregrounds its subject without specifying an external agent. N4:grammar:supp-nasaru-honorific.notes: なさる honors another person's する action; polite なさいます and te-form なさって. The third example お気をつけてお帰りなさい uses the separate お + verb stem + なさい request construction, not an inflected なさる. It asks the person to take care going home.

N4:grammar:supp-sorede-and-then.notes: それで connects a preceding situation with its result, or prompts continuation of a story. It is not merely interchangeable with temporal それから. In the third example どうしましたか asks what the addressee did next. The first example describes a delayed train causing late arrival at the meeting.

examples.en: The train was delayed. As a result, I was late to the meeting.

examples.ja: 昨日は疲れていました。それで、早く寝ました。
examples.en: I was tired yesterday. So I went to bed early.

examples.ja: それで、どうしましたか。
examples.en: And then, what did you do?

corrections.original: それで is a sentence-initial conjunction meaning 'and then / so / as a result'. It connects a previous event or reason to a consequent event or action, but with a more narrative / sequential feel than だから. Often used to introduce the next step in a story or to prompt someone to continue ('and then?'). More neutral tone than だから.
corrections.replacement: それで connects a preceding situation with its result, or prompts continuation of a story. It is not merely interchangeable with temporal それから. In the third example どうしましたか asks what the addressee did next. The first example describes a delayed train causing late arrival at the meeting.

corrections.original: And then, what happened?
corrections.replacement: And then, what did you do?

source_corrections.basis: Resultative connector not merely sequence; delayed train not cancelled, arrival late not meeting held late. Yesterday past early bedtime not today/morning; dou-shimashita action question more exact than generic what happened.

corrections.original: はず expresses the speaker's expectation based on reasoning or evidence — 'it should be' or 'it ought to be'. Unlike かもしれない (possibility), はず implies stronger certainty; unlike べき (obligation), はず is about expectation rather than what someone should do morally. The negative はずがない means 'there's no way that' — a strong denial.
corrections.replacement: はず states an expectation derived from known facts or reasoning, not an obligation; the expectation can disagree with reality. はずがない / はずはない strongly deny that the proposition could hold. Do not translate an expected arrival as a command to arrive.

source_corrections.basis: Hazu reasoned expectation not obligation; na-adjective na vs noun no source error corrected. Today affirmative expected arrival and tomorrow parcel not past negative; sonna-hazu-wa-nai strong denial.

corrections.replacement: Prohibits doing the action: must not / not allowed. This is not lack of necessity (do not have to). Casual contraction depends on whether the verb te-form ends in て or で.

N4:grammar:supp-ga-kedo-although.notes: が / けど / けれども connect contrasting clauses or soften a preface to a request or explanation. が is also common in polite conversation, not restricted to writing; けど is relatively informal. Present affirmative noun/na-adjective clauses retain the copula before the conjunction: 学生だけど. A strong contrast is not required in every use.

corrections.original: が, けど, and けれども are conjunctions meaning 'but' or 'although'. They connect two clauses with a contrastive relationship. が is slightly more formal and written; けど is casual spoken; けれども is formal. They are also often used as soft sentence openers without a strong contrastive meaning — 'well…' or 'by the way…'.
corrections.replacement: が / けど / けれども connect contrasting clauses or soften a preface to a request or explanation. が is also common in polite conversation, not restricted to writing; けど is relatively informal. Present affirmative noun/na-adjective clauses retain the copula before the conjunction: 学生だけど. A strong contrast is not required in every use.

source_corrections.basis: Difficult but interesting; desire to go blocked by no time, not time affirmative invented quotation; costly past and glad bought not cost increased. Copula retained before kedo and soft-introduction use.

N4:grammar:supp-ni-naru-become.formation: Noun / na-adjective + に + なる. I-adjective: remove final い + くなる; 高い → 高くなる. いい → よくなる.
N4:grammar:supp-ni-naru-become.notes: なる foregrounds a change of state; it does not guarantee that the change is natural, gradual or without human intervention. する foregrounds bringing something into a state. くなってきた presents change developing up to the present.

corrections.original: Noun/な-adj + に + なる. い-adj: drop い, add くなる.
corrections.replacement: Noun / na-adjective + に + なる. I-adjective: remove final い + くなる; 高い → 高くなる. いい → よくなる.

corrections.original: なる means 'to become', expressing a natural or gradual change. For nouns and な-adjectives, the pattern is X + に + なる. For い-adjectives, drop い and add くなる (高い → 高くなる). The change is framed as happening on its own, as opposed to being caused by someone (for which use する).
corrections.replacement: なる foregrounds a change of state; it does not guarantee that the change is natural, gradual or without human intervention. する foregrounds bringing something into a state. くなってきた presents change developing up to the present.

source_corrections.basis: Become not likeness/static doctor or mere cold; change up to now te-kuru and improved Japanese not inability of Japan. Naru does not guarantee spontaneity/gradualness; ii→yoku formation.

N4:grammar:supp-owaru-finish.formation: Verb masu-stem + 終わる (godan), e.g. 読み終わる. Some compounds also use 終える (ichidan), e.g. やり終える.
N4:grammar:supp-owaru-finish.notes: A compound marks completing an action. Standalone 終わる is intransitive, but a compound such as 本を読み終わる retains the first verb's object. 終える is not a mechanical replacement in every compound. The final example requests a phone call after finishing the movie; the Japanese does not specify the recipient.

examples.ja: 本を読み終わりました。
examples.en: I finished reading the book.

examples.ja: 宿題をやり終えた。
examples.en: I finished the homework. (plain)

examples.ja: 映画を見終わったら、電話してください。
examples.en: Please call when you finish watching the movie.

corrections.original: Verb stem + 終わる (or + 終える for transitive nuance).
corrections.replacement: Verb masu-stem + 終わる (godan), e.g. 読み終わる. Some compounds also use 終える (ichidan), e.g. やり終える.

corrections.original: 終わる attached to a verb stem forms a compound meaning 'finish doing X'. It is the completion counterpart to 始める. The standalone verb 終わる means 'to end' or 'to be over'. Note that 終える (transitive) can also be used: verb-stem + 終える.
corrections.replacement: A compound marks completing an action. Standalone 終わる is intransitive, but a compound such as 本を読み終わる retains the first verb's object. 終える is not a mechanical replacement in every compound. The final example requests a phone call after finishing the movie; the Japanese does not specify the recipient.

corrections.original: Please call me when you finish watching the movie.
corrections.replacement: Please call when you finish watching the movie.

source_corrections.basis: Completion not starting to read; school homework not housework; conditional completion before call request restored. Japanese does not specify call recipient so unsupported me removed from English. Compound transitivity not standalone owaru rule.

corrections.original: easy to ___
corrections.replacement: easy to do; also prone / likely to occur depending on context

corrections.original: Verb stem + やすい
corrections.replacement: Verb masu-stem + やすい; inflect as an i-adjective: やすくない, やすかった.

corrections.original: やすい attached to a verb stem creates an い-adjective meaning 'easy to do X'. It describes the intrinsic ease of doing something, often a property of the object of the action ('this pen is easy to write with').
corrections.replacement: やすい can express ease of doing an action or a tendency for an event to occur. Ease can depend on an object, circumstances or the person; it is not solely an intrinsic property. corrections.replacement: Verb masu-stem + にくい; inflect as an i-adjective: にくかった, にくくない.

corrections.original: にくい attached to a verb stem creates an い-adjective meaning 'hard to do X'. It is the opposite of やすい. Note that a stronger form づらい exists, sometimes with a nuance of physical or emotional difficulty.

corrections.replacement: This writing is hard to read.

N4:grammar:supp-garu-third-person-emotio.formation: Suitable i-adjective: remove final い + がる, e.g. 寒がる, 嬉しがる, 痛がる, 欲しがる. Desire たい: remove final い + がる, e.g. 食べたがる. Some na-adjectives also occur, e.g. 嫌がる. Lexical compatibility matters.
N4:grammar:supp-garu-third-person-emotio.notes: がる commonly presents another person's observable emotion or desire; it does not mean every third-person feeling must use this form. Quotation, evidential expressions and narrative permit other ways to describe another's inner state. Current signs commonly use がっている; がる can describe disposition or repeated behavior. It conjugates as a godan verb.

corrections.original: i-adj: drop い, add がる: 寒い → 寒がる, 嬉しい → 嬉しがる, 痛い → 痛がる. 〜たい form: drop い, add がる: 食べたい → 食べたがる (see tagaru-third-person-desire).
corrections.replacement: Suitable i-adjective: remove final い + がる, e.g. 寒がる, 嬉しがる, 痛がる, 欲しがる. Desire たい: remove final い + がる, e.g. 食べたがる. Some na-adjectives also occur, e.g. 嫌がる. Lexical compatibility matters.

corrections.original: 〜がる attaches to an adjective or a 〜たい form to express that a third person appears to feel a certain emotion, based on their observable behavior. Japanese treats one's own inner states (〜い, 〜たい) and the inner states of others differently: you can state your own feelings directly, but you must describe others' feelings as behaviorally observable — hence 〜がる ('show signs of being X'). Conjugates as a godan u-verb.
corrections.replacement: がる commonly presents another person's observable emotion or desire; it does not mean every third-person feeling must use this form. Quotation, evidential expressions and narrative permit other ways to describe another's inner state. Current signs commonly use がっている; がる can describe disposition or repeated behavior. It conjugates as a godan verb.

source_corrections.basis: Unrelated political Nepali removed. Younger brother not son/grandson, summer even cold sensitivity; woman wants child and dog walk not narrator travel. Observable desire and current/habitual distinction; not compulsory garu for every third-person statement.

N4:grammar:supp-mae-ni-before-doing.formation: Basic affirmative temporal pattern: verb dictionary (non-past) form + 前に; noun + の前に.
N4:grammar:supp-mae-ni-before-doing.notes: In this basic affirmative pattern the before-clause uses the dictionary form even if the main event is past: 日本に来る前に日本語を勉強しました. Preserve the order of the two events. This explanation is not a universal ban on every other negative or discourse construction containing 前に.

corrections.replacement: Basic affirmative temporal pattern: verb dictionary (non-past) form + 前に; noun + の前に.

corrections.original: 〜前に marks a temporal 'before' clause. The verb in the 前に clause is ALWAYS in dictionary (plain non-past) form, regardless of whether the main clause describes a past, present, or future event — this is a common error point for learners who want to match tenses. For noun references, use noun + の + 前に.
corrections.replacement: In this basic affirmative pattern the before-clause uses the dictionary form even if the main event is past: 日本に来る前に日本語を勉強しました. Preserve the order of the two events. This explanation is not a universal ban on every other negative or discourse construction containing 前に.

source_corrections.basis: Before not during/after, imperative handwashing not negative washing, teeth brushing not teeth cold; past study precedes coming Japan not going at same time. Basic affirmative dictionary-form relative tense qualified, not universal ban on every negative clause.

N4:grammar:supp-koto-ni-suru-decide.formation: Dictionary form + ことにする; nai-form + ことにする. Past decision ことにした. Maintained self-rule/habit in this use: ことにしている.
N4:grammar:supp-koto-ni-suru-decide.notes: ことにする foregrounds the decision-maker's choice, not only decisions by the speaker. ことになる foregrounds the resulting decision or arrangement; it is not a morphological passive. In the second example ことにしている expresses a self-imposed continuing rule, not a decision currently in progress.

corrections.original: V plain non-past + ことにする (decide to); V ない + ことにする (decide not to); past: ことにした; progressive: ことにしている.
corrections.replacement: Dictionary form + ことにする; nai-form + ことにする. Past decision ことにした. Maintained self-rule/habit in this use: ことにしている.

corrections.original: 〜ことにする expresses an active personal decision made by the speaker — 'I decided to do X'. Distinct from its passive counterpart 〜ことになる ('it has been decided'), where the decision comes from circumstance or others. The progressive form 〜ことにしている expresses a habitual decision or self-rule ('I make it a habit to'). Past form 〜ことにした = 'decided'.
corrections.replacement: ことにする foregrounds the decision-maker's choice, not only decisions by the speaker. ことになる foregrounds the resulting decision or arrangement; it is not a morphological passive. In the second example ことにしている expresses a self-imposed continuing rule, not a decision currently in progress.

source_corrections.basis: Decision not mere wanting, tomorrow onward daily exercise not completed daily practice, sweets not white/food and negative self-rule kept; study abroad decided. Naru not morphological passive, no speaker-only rule.

N4:grammar:supp-koto-ni-naru-be-decided.formation: Dictionary form / nai-form + ことになる. Decided arrangement: ことになった. Established rule, custom or schedule in this use: ことになっている.

corrections.replacement: Dictionary form / nai-form + ことになる. Decided arrangement: ことになった. Established rule, custom or schedule in this use: ことになっている.

corrections.original: 〜ことになる expresses that a decision has been made by circumstance or others, without the speaker's direct agency — 'it was decided that X'. corrections.replacement: ことになる foregrounds an outcome, decision or arrangement without foregrounding who decided; it does not guarantee the speaker had no part in deciding. ことになっている can express an established rule, custom or schedule. 転勤 is a job transfer, not merely travel or moving residence.

source_corrections.basis: Tokyo not India, job transfer not generic move and no invented quotation. Shoes removed before home entry, meeting next week decided not obligation to decide. De-emphasized agency not absolute exclusion, established custom.

N4:grammar:supp-nasai-command.meaning: do it — directive commonly used from an authority position
N4:grammar:supp-nasai-command.notes: Masu-stem + なさい is common from parents to children, teachers to students, and in written instructions. corrections.replacement: Masu-stem + なさい is common from parents to children, teachers to students, and in written instructions. It can sound less abrupt than a bare imperative but is not inherently gentle. It is not a general substitute for polite adult requests; the issue is authority and relationship, not merely casual register.

source_corrections.basis: Commands not first-person future/past polite statements. Early/quick wake left broad via chito/taratari, homework not housework, vegetables not generic meal. Not inherently gentle; authority not merely casualness.

N4:grammar:supp-ageru-give-outward.meaning: give to another person / being (giver-oriented perspective)
N4:grammar:supp-ageru-give-outward.notes: あげる can describe the speaker giving to another, or one third party giving to another; the giver need not always be in the speaker's in-group. Giving toward the speaker normally uses くれる. In respectful contexts さしあげる or reformulation may be appropriate depending on relationship and situation, not a universal ban on every use involving a superior. Preserve giver が/は, recipient に and thing を.

corrections.original: to give (outward, from in-group to out-group)
corrections.replacement: give to another person / being (giver-oriented perspective)

corrections.original: あげる is the basic verb for 'give', used when the giver is the speaker or in-group and the receiver is outside that group. Crucially, do NOT use あげる when giving TO yourself (use くれる in that direction), and do NOT use あげる for superiors (use さしあげる or reformulate). The full giving-verb system is: あげる (outward), くれる (toward speaker), もらう (receive).
corrections.replacement: あげる can describe the speaker giving to another, or one third party giving to another; the giver need not always be in the speaker's in-group. Giving toward the speaker normally uses くれる.
